newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Enerco 96/7 forecasts still valid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Enerco 96/7 forecasts still valid.

text.p: Enerco New Zealand Ltd Chief Executive Kevin Johnson said on Wednesday the company's profit forecast of NZ$18.75-$19.25 million for the year to March, 1997, was still valid.

Johnson also told Reuters in an interview that the number of new customers added over the year would be close to the gas distribution firm's projection of 10,000, and that that kind of growth appeared sustainable for the next few years.
Enerco Chairman John Gray made the profit forecast at the company's annual meeting last July, and in the company's annual report released earlier.
Asked if the profit forecast was still valid, Johnson said: "We haven't revised that estimate so it still stands."
Enerco added 6,100 residential customers in the year to March 1995.
"In the financial year that has just finished we have forecast about 10,000 so we should be pretty close to it, which is quite significant growth," Johnson said.
Enerco now has about 100,000 customers, but Johnson said there would at some point be an optimum level of penetration.
"We are some way off that yet in Auckland. We are pretty close to that level in Palmerston North and Wellington and more growth is available in Hawkes Bay.

"But in Auckland, which is our real growth market, there is still the opportunity for growth, so the sort of levels we achieved in the financial year just gone are sustainable for another few years, but obviously there is a limit," he said.
Johnson said the gas distributor, which operates either complete or near monopolies in several North Island regions, did not see the prospect of increased competition as a major threat.
"There may be some loss of business but in fact the more people that are out there selling gas the better," he said.
Prospective competitors in many cases would need to use the Enerco network to transport their product, he noted.
Enerco, 69 percent owned by Christchurch based Southpower, made a NZ$16.25 million profit in the year to March 1996 and paid a total dividend for the year of 14.5 cents per share.
Its shares traded at $6.00 by 3.00 pm (0300 GMT)on Wednesday.
